title: Slimline trace adapter and metric cardinality migration
creator: Ana Patel
description: Refactor the current tracing and metrics adapters to reduce allocation pressure and cut cardinality on high-volume tags. Goals: upgrade OpenTelemetry libraries, replace the legacy trace shim with a lightweight zero-copy adapter, introduce attribute sanitization and enumeration for high-cardinality fields, and migrate histogram metrics to pre-bucket aggregation to reduce scrapes and ingestion costs. Deliverables: (1) otel adapter v2 (zero-copy span/context propagation); (2) metric migration plan and name map; (3) benchmark results vs baseline; (4) rollout/canary plan with feature flags. This work targets runtime-1.20 release and Dedicated telemetry backends. Rationale: production clusters are hitting 15-30% CPU overhead from span creation and metrics encoding under peak load; high-cardinality tags in request attributes are a major driver of cardinality explosions in our observability billing.
comments: 2026-01-21 — Spike complete: prototyped zero-copy span wrapper using mutable buffers. Raw benchmark vs mainline: 24% CPU reduction on synthetic 200 qps load, 18% fewer allocations per request. Artifact: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/compare/zero-copy-spans

2026-01-25 — Architecture sync with infra and runtime teams. Decided to keep current OTLP wire format but change exporter batching and compress payloads at exporter level to amortize cost. Trade-off: increases exporter code complexity but avoids cross-service protocol changes.

2026-01-30 — Design review feedback from PM (Sofia Gómez): require a migration table for metric names and a short retention of deprecated metric aliases for 6 weeks to avoid dashboard breakage. Added to scope.

2026-02-03 — QA notes: added unit tests for attribute sanitizer (rules for user_id, email, ip -> hashed or removed) and e2e test against local jaeger collector. Observed an edge-case where internal debug tag `request.debug.trace_id` was being dropped; created follow-up sub-issue ENG-33453 to scope whitelisting for internal debug fields.

2026-02-08 — Benchmarks after OTEL upgrade to 1.17.0: span export latency P95 reduced by 12ms under 500qps when exporter batching enabled; memory allocation reduced by ~22% in the agent. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482

2026-02-11 — Security review: determined no new PII is introduced; sanitizer rules approved. Logging & audit checklist completed. security_review_required set to true for final rollout because metric migrations touch compliance dashboards.
